Hi Sam — quick technical note based on the numbers above and our internal microbenchmarks (attached):

Short answers:
- Streaming: yes — our runtime supports token-by-token streaming for the model families you mentioned, with negligible additional tail cost (we keep KV cache on-GPU and stream from the host only for network egress).
- Per-GPU reserved throughput (observed):
  - A100-80GB: ~35 short-form req/s (p95 ~220ms under steady-state for 1K-token-ish prompts)
  - H100-80GB: ~55 short-form req/s (p95 ~160ms under steady-state)
- For mixed workloads (70/30 short/long): we recommend planning for effective capacity using token-weighted throughput. Conservatively, an H100 slot can sustain ~40 effective concurrent sessions with the distribution you gave while holding p95 short-form < 250ms.

Sizing suggestion for your SLOs and peak concurrency (~500 concurrent burst):
- Baseline reserved: 12 H100 slots (12 * 40 = 480 effective concurrent short-form equivalents) to meet sustained load with headroom.
- Burst: add autoscale buffer of +25% (3 additional slots) to absorb sudden bursts to 500.
- If you must use A100 for cost reasons, plan ~18 A100 slots with similar buffer.

Notes and caveats:
- Tail behavior: p99 may spike on long sequences; we recommend enabling per-request streaming to keep perceived latency low and using our KV-prefix caching for repeated prompt prefixes.
- Network egress from your VPC may add 20–60ms depending on path; during the joint test please capture packet traces and agent logs.
- We'll run a dedicated end-to-end validation using your representative prompt set (Marissa, please share final prompt set and traffic profile).

I attached the short internal benchmark PDF and the raw CSV for reference. Rafael / Neha — adding you in case you want to adjust recommended slot counts or the autoscale policy.
